messages:
Eve (CS): Heads-up — I'm putting together a short customer-facing runbook for onboarding that focuses on caching, batching, and streaming. Goal: lower early token costs and keep latency under trial SLOs. Can we land on a minimal set of recommended defaults + 1–2 copy-paste config examples? cc @Jordan (SE) @Priya (Product)

Jordan (SE): Draft below — feel free to copy into the onboarding doc. Kept it concise for customer consumption.

Jordan (SE): RUNBOOK (customer-facing, short) — Purpose: help trial and early-production customers reduce token spend and avoid latency spikes.
1) When to enable prefix/KV caching:
  - Use when request patterns show repeated prefixes (chatbots, instruction templates, system prompts).
  - Not for single-shot varied prompts (e.g., open-ended search).
  - Enable early for trials that have >10 requests/min with repeating prompts.

2) Recommended caching defaults (customer-visible):
  - Prefix cache TTL: 24h (extend to 7d for stable assistant use).
  - Max cached prefixes: 5k per tenant.
  - Cache hit goal: >40% for cost savings to be material.
  - Eviction policy: LRU with write-through persistence for Dedicated.

3) Batching guidance:
  - When to batch: high throughput automated requests (embeddings, bulk reranks, high-traffic chat).
  - Default batch window: 20–50ms (start 30ms).
  - Max batch tokens: 32k tokens across requests or 8k tokens/request (whichever hits first).
  - Prefer server-side continuous batching where possible; client-side buffering OK for non-interactive workloads.

4) Streaming best-practices:
  - Chunk size: 256–512 tokens per flush for medium models, 128 for low-latency small models.
  - Flush interval: 50–150ms. Tune down if UI needs quicker partial responses.
  - Backpressure: honor client ACKs; drop large buffered payloads to avoid OOM.

5) Monitoring + alerting (What to watch):
  - Token cost per session, p50/p95 latency, cache hit rate, batch fill ratio.
  - Alert thresholds: p95 latency > target +30% for 15m, cache hit < 25% for 1h for inference-heavy products.

6) Fallbacks + renewal-risk playbook:
  - If trial account shows sustained high latency or token cost and low engagement: schedule enablement call within 48h.
  - Auto-fallback: route to cheaper model variant or increase batching when latency SLO breached.
  - Renewal flag: >25% increase in estimated monthly cost vs baseline and <10% month-over-month feature usage growth.

EXAMPLES customers can paste quickly:

Customer config — caching + batching example (SDK pseudocode):
```json
{
  "cache": {
    "enabled": true,
    "prefix_ttl": "24h",
    "max_prefixes": 5000
  },
  "batching": {
    "enabled": true,
    "batch_window_ms": 30,
    "max_batch_tokens": 32000
  },
  "streaming": {
    "chunk_tokens": 256,
    "flush_interval_ms": 100
  }
}
```

Curl streaming example (for UI teams):
```bash
curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-medium", "stream": true, "prompt":"Hello"}' \
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate | while read line; do echo "$line"; done
```

Jordan (SE): Quick ops note — ask customers to enable token/latency sampling in Redwood Console and share a 24h export during onboarding call. We can then suggest tuned TTLs and batch windows.

Priya (Product): Add to that renewal-risk rubric: for commercial trials, if predicted monthly invoice > $5k and cache hit < 30%, flag for CS + Solutions Eng for proactive cost optimization enablement. Also include a short customer-facing paragraph explaining why caching helps safety & privacy: reduced model exposure for repeated system prompts.

Luis (Eng): Implementation notes for Dedicated/Private customers: prefer persistent KV (Redis or local SSD-backed) with write-through to avoid cold-start misses after restarts. For Hosted customers, recommend our managed prefix caching with 24h default but allow customers to opt into 7d TTL for steady workloads.

OnboardBot: Runbook page created: /internal/cs/runbooks/caching-batching-streaming — shared with Customer Success and Solutions Eng.

Eve (CS): This is perfect — I'll take the SDK snippet + the short rubric into the onboarding checklist. Plan: include a one-page PDF in our trial welcome pack and ask customers to run the Console export before the first enablement call.

Eve (CS): Action items: @Jordan to post a copy of the runnable SDK snippet to the doc, @Luis to confirm Dedicated persistence note, @Priya to add the renewal flag thresholds. Recommend we schedule a 30m sync this week to finalize. :handshake: :rocket:
